reported.title: pH value never converted from millivolts
reported.description: computePh() at lines 21-24 simply returns the millivolt value unchanged instead of dividing by 500, so lastPh holds millivolts rather than pH. The measured output confirms this: the firmware printed 3670.58 pH while the injected input was 7.21 to 7.41 pH, off by 3663.2 pH, and 9 of 9 values were wrong. Firmware printed 3670.58 pH at 1.01 s while the injected input was 7.21 to 7.41 pH: off by 3663.2 pH (tolerance ±0.2). 9 of 9 values were wrong.

reported.title: Alert LED compares millivolts to pH threshold, never asserts
reported.description: Because computePh() returns millivolts (lines 21-24), the comparison at line 66 compares a millivolt-scale value against ALERT_PH = 7.20, which is always true, so D13 stays LOW. The measured evidence shows D13 was not HIGH for 1270 ms while required during the nominal ramp, and for 2000 ms in the glitch scenario. D13 was in the wrong state for 4850 ms across 6 interval(s), first at 500 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 500 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

judge_input.spec:
- Linearized pH probe on A0 with scale 500 mV/pH (0 mV → pH 0.0); low-pH alert LED on D13.
- Convert ADC samples using a 5.000 V / 1023 full-scale span, then divide millivolts by 500 to obtain pH.
- Print exactly one line every 1000 ms matching `pH: <value>` with two decimal places.
- Printed pH must stay within ±0.20 of the injected probe value.
- Drive D13 HIGH when reported pH is below 7.20; otherwise drive D13 LOW.
- Keep logging while the alert LED is on or off.
